name: Punish the early queen
description: Develop with tempo against a queen that came out too soon.

lessons.prompt: White threatens mate. Stop it and hit the queen at the same time.
hints: A pawn move that blocks the queen’s path to f7 and attacks it.
lessons.explanation: 3...g6 stops Qxf7# and attacks the queen. After 4.Qf3 Nf6 Black develops with gain of time. Careful: 3...Nf6?? loses to 4.Qxf7#.

lessons.prompt: The queen is in the middle of the board. Develop and attack it.
hints: Which piece can develop with a threat?
lessons.explanation: 3.Nc3 develops with tempo: the queen must move again and White gains time. That is the basic problem of the Scandinavian.

lessons.prompt: White’s queen recaptured on move 3. Make it pay.
hints: Which piece develops with a threat?
lessons.explanation: 3...Nc6 develops and attacks the queen, so White spends another move on it. That is why the Center Game is rare.

lessons.prompt: Same story in the Philidor. Develop with tempo.
hints: The queen on d4 can be attacked.
lessons.explanation: 4...Nc6 develops and hits the queen. That is why White usually recaptures with the knight (4.Nxd4) instead.

lessons.prompt: White took back with the queen. Gain a tempo.
lessons.explanation: 4...Nc6 gains time on the queen. 4.Qxd4 is playable for White (5.Bb5 pins the knight), but Black develops comfortably.
